svg.text: the layers an operator passes through. A stage name is declared once and stops at the DAG; below it nothing reads one.
stage names live here only: vocabulary, wave plan, colocation rules
which is why it carries work_conserving = False
what the builders emit for the MegaMoE vocabulary (five stages, one event per tile):
tile cost d(e) = max( MAC(e) / rate_cube , bytes(e) / BW(link) ) — compute and movement are two costs of one event, never two boxes
the scheduler reads the five fields and nothing else. Contention, colocation and buffer credits are what make time.
cube = dark, vector = light, link = outline. An event may hold several resources at once; t_base then takes max over all of them.
free(r) } that the credits A(e) admit.
A concrete resource takes the max of the set; a pool placeholder such as AIC:* takes the min, which is what late binding means.
activation carries colocate_with, so it must take the core its gmm1 tile already holds: a free core elsewhere cannot help it, which is why
pinned roles are excluded from the idle test. The wave boundary is a credit, not an edge: dispatch w1 releases an L1 slot and gmm1 t3 is admitted.
a schedule is only read off once it clears two tests that do not depend on the orchestration being modelled.
All three move with the shape
alone, so T̂ under any of them
idle on a pooled role, per core:
avoidable_idle_us — something was ready while a
avoidable is an upper bound, not a ledger: under
phase pipelining the phase group inflates it, and
roles pinned by colocate_with or core_group are
excluded by derivation from the graph, not by hand.
change exactly one knob — tile size, wave split, steal driver, binding — and re-run
ΔT̂ is the cost of that one choice: both runs are scheduled from the same declarations and pass the same two tests, so neither is fitted to the other.
